exposure: staff education and production of clinical guidelines
cohort: 200 cases of cesarean section (100 from October 2014 and 100 from February 2015)
finding: A high number of unnecessary cesarean sections were performed, likely due to lack of knowledge and inexperience of staff, indicating a need for systemic change in healthcare resources, education, and clinical governance.
mod_finding: The study found that the most common indication for cesarean section was dystocia (43.5%), followed by fetal distress (18.5%), previous scar (17%), malpresentation (10.5%), and maternal compromise (10%).
